podcast.title: "Alternative" Music Definition
podcast.body: Blackfire described their music as "alternative" not just for its sound, but because its subject matter consistently deals with critical native concerns such as human rights, genocide, environmental issues, and domestic violence. "They liked to call their music alternative because while the sound is alternative, the subject matter deals with native concerns like human rights and genocide, environmental issues, domestic violence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: All-Ages Venue Preference
podcast.body: The band made an effort to play exclusively at all-ages venues, indicating a desire to reach a broad audience and engage with younger fans. "They tried to play only all ages venues."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaborations with Ramones Circle
podcast.body: The band has worked with members of the Ramones Circle, indicating a connection to the punk rock lineage and influence from the iconic band. "They work with members of the Ramones Circle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founding and Release History
podcast.body: Blackfire was founded in 1989 and has released a series of EPs and albums sporadically throughout their career. "Blackfire was founded in 1989 and have sporadically released a series of EPs and albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Navajo Nation Origins
podcast.body: Blackfire is a punk and alternative rock band from Phoenix, Arizona, consisting of two brothers and a sister, all of whom are members of the Arizona Navajo Nation, specifically the Diné. "Two brothers and a sister, all from the Arizona Navajo Nation, the DNA to be specific."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Traditional and Modern Influences
podcast.body: Their father was a traditional medicine man who ensured his children were familiar with their tribe's music, while also being supportive of their love for bands like the Ramones. This unique upbringing influenced their blend of sound and subject matter. "Their father was a traditional medicine man who also made sure his kids knew about the tribe's music. He also did not mind that the kids really really liked bands like the Ramones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
